purpose: Which of the flow-truth review's 29 findings the rebuilt package's test suite actually asserts, and which it does not. The review is a record and is never edited; this declares, from outside it, what a tracked source has since established about each finding. As of 2026-09-15 all 29 are covered.
whyThisExists: docs/deployment/OUTSTANDING_SOURCES.json has said since 2026-09-14 that all 29 findings stay counted open because 'tests/flow-truth-persistence.test.mjs names this review — but that suite asserts no finding by id, so nothing establishes which.' The suite has 51 assertions and cites zero finding ids, so the estate could not tell which findings the rebuild answered and which it left. That is the single largest tractable piece of the 56 open items with no stated closure criterion.
whatCoveredMeans: An assertion in the suite fails if the defect the finding names is present in the rebuilt package. It does NOT mean the finding was wrong, and it does not resolve anything about the tenant: B1's three lists still do not exist, and the suite asserts that the package says so rather than pretending otherwise. Covered means the PACKAGE defect the finding raises is now held closed by a gate. Closing the last seven found one finding still live: C11, which the rebuild had not fixed and which no assertion would have caught.

findings.title: The three target lists exist nowhere in the estate
via: the companion states the provisioning state the capture supports
no GUID is claimed for a resource nobody has built
findings.note: The package no longer writes to lists it cannot address: it declares BLOCKED-ON-PROVISIONING and claims no GUID. The lists themselves are still unbuilt — that is Step 5 of the governance runbook, tracked separately, and this finding does not track it.

findings.title: Lists are targeted by display title, not by GUID
via: no GUID is claimed for a resource nobody has built
findings.note: Targets resolve through docs/deployment/governance/list-bindings.json, which maps title to GUID and holds null until the list is built. The assertion fails if a GUID is invented for an unbuilt resource.

findings.title: Every stored URL is broken by the first space
via: C9 · no item column stores a URL, so none can be broken by the first space in one
findings.note: Answered by absence, which is the stronger answer: the rebuild stores no URL at all. The assertion keeps it that way, because a URL column added later would reintroduce the escaping problem the finding names.

findings.title: ComplianceIssuesJson stores notification delivery
via: C10 · every Compliance column reads the governance input, not notification delivery
findings.note: The rebuild already read the governance input; nothing asserted it, so a later edit could have put anything in a declared column.

findings.title: Three columns carry the wrong identity
via: C11 · EnvironmentName is written by nothing — a flow cannot read a display name, and the identifier is not one
findings.note: THE ONE THE REBUILD HAD NOT FIXED. It wrote EnvironmentName from the same expression as EnvironmentId, so the column the design calls a human-readable name held an identifier — C11 verbatim, still live on 2026-09-15. A flow has one environment designator and it is not a display name, so the column is now written by nothing. Optional in the design, so leaving it empty is what the spec permits.

findings.title: Three columns carry the wrong identity
via: C12 · FlowName reads the display name, never
findings.note: Already correct in the rebuild; now gated.

findings.title: contentSizeBytes is a character count
via: every manifest entry records the ETag and byte size SharePoint returned
findings.note: The size now comes from body/Size — what SharePoint returned — rather than from length() over a string.

findings.title: An append-only list with no index strategy
via: every $filter leads on a unique, indexed key
findings.note: The suite's own comment states the reason: this is the only shape that survives a list past the 5,000-item view threshold, which an append-only ledger reaches by definition.

findings.title: A null HTML report aborts the chain after two files are written
via: C16 · no file creation runs after another
findings.note: The rebuild replaced the series with a fan-out from the run folder, so a null report cannot strand the others half-written. The citation is the invariant half of the label: the assertion interpolates the count of file actions, so quoting the rendered text would break the moment a file is added.
findings.viaPattern: C16 · no file creation runs after another

findings.title: Four timestamps from four separate utcNow() calls
via: C17 · the persisted record calls utcNow() nowhere — its times read one captured value
findings.note: The seven utcNow() calls that remain are in seven different actions at seven different moments, which is legitimate. What C17 names is one RECORD disagreeing with itself, and the record now reads capturedUtc from Compose_Persistence_Identity alone.

findings.title: Scope_Persistence_Failure does not cover Skipped

via: C18 · the final Compose accepts Skipped from the failure scope, so a clean run still reports
